### Import Library
```{r}
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
```
### Reading Data
> Dataset: examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv
```{r}
#| warning: false
nhanes <- read_csv('examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv')
head(nhanes)
colnames(nhanes)
```

### Define and document an analysis cohort using age 20-80
> Filtering the data based on `Age` range to records with age from 20 through 80, inclusive. Missing BMI and income group were counted before complete-case rows were selected for the grouped results.

```{r}
#| warning: false

adult_cohort <- nhanes |>
  filter(Age >= 20, Age <= 80) |>
    mutate(IncomeGroup = factor(IncomeGroup, 
         levels = c("Low Income (<1.3)", 
                    "Middle Income", 
                    "High Income (>3.5)")),
         MaritalClean = factor(MaritalClean, 
                               levels = c("Married/Partner", 
                               "Previously Married",
                               "Never Married" 
                               ))) 

cohort_counts <- tibble(step = c("Prepared data", "After age 20-80 restriction"),
  n = c(nrow(nhanes), nrow(adult_cohort)))

kable(cohort_counts)
```

### Create a missingness table for key variables.
> Key variables are defined as: `BMI`, `Age`, `IncomeGroup`, `Gender`, `MaritalClean`, `Race`, and `Cycle`.
```{r}
#| warning: false

key_vars <- c("BMI", "Age", "IncomeGroup", "Gender", "MaritalClean", "Race", "Cycle")

missingness <- tibble(variable = key_vars) |>
  mutate(
    missing_n = vapply(
      adult_cohort[key_vars],
      function(x) sum(is.na(x)),
      numeric(1)
    ),
    missing_percent = round(100 * missing_n / nrow(adult_cohort), 1)
  )

write_csv(
  missingness,
  "assignments/assignment06-eda-ai-audit/submission/missingness-summary.csv")

kable(missingness)
```

### Produce a Table 1-style summary by IncomeGroup.
>  The following Table-1-style table uses rows with **non-missing** age and BMI while grouping by income groups after applying the age restriction. 

> * Include a caption to the table.
```{r}
#| warning: false

complete_analysis <- adult_cohort |>
  filter(!is.na(Age), !is.na(BMI), !is.na(IncomeGroup))

table1 <- complete_analysis |>
  group_by(IncomeGroup) |>
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    `BMI, mean (SD)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(BMI), sd(BMI)),
    `BMI, median (SD)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", median(BMI), sd(BMI)),
    `Age, mean (SD)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(Age), sd(Age)),
    `Age, median (SD)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", median(Age), sd(Age)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

write_csv(
  table1,
  "assignments/assignment06-eda-ai-audit/submission/table1.csv"
)

kable(table1,
caption = "Table 1. Unweighted count for each income group with average and median summary with respective standard deviation of each income group")
```

### Preliminary Figure
> Produce a preliminary exploratory figure that displays the Mean BMI across all available NHANES cylcle for adults age 20-80 based on different Income Groups. Overclaims about the data should be avoided.
```{r}
#| warning: false

cycle_summary <- complete_analysis |>
  filter(!is.na(Cycle)) |>
  group_by(Cycle, IncomeGroup) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_bmi = mean(BMI),
    .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n >= 30) 
cycle_summary

ggplot(cycle_summary,
  aes(x = Cycle, y = mean_bmi, color = IncomeGroup, group = IncomeGroup)
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  expand_limits(y = 0) +
  labs(
    title = "Unweighted BMI average by income group across NHANES cycle",
    subtitle = "Adults age 20-80; prepared example classroom data",
    x = "NHANES cycle",
    y = "Mean BMI (kg/m²; unweighted)",
    color = "Income group"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "top"
  )
```


### Write a short methods note stating that the analysis is descriptive, unweighted, and non-causal.
* The summaries are descriptive, unweighted, and non-causal. The summaries and figure produced above do not account for the NHANES survey design (i.e., weights were not applied to calculation), do not estimate the US adult population, and do not show that different income causes BMI differences. Missing BMI or income-group records from surveyed adults are not included in the grouped results.

### Audit the planted-error starter and list at least five issues.
1.  The data is not being imported using a relative path, meaning that collaborators or other auditors will not be able to replicate running the same code.
2. The original author wrote that the age-restriction applied to the date would be adults age 20-80 inclusive, but their code doesn't capture the inclusive part (i.e., they filtered the age but excluded the lower limit 20 and the upper limit 80.)
3. Did not disclose and describe their NA null value omission. 
4. Did not write up a caption to describe the summary table for their Table-1-style summary.
5. The original author claimed that, "The differences in BMI between income groups are **statistically significant**, which shows that income determines BMI". The first problem with this statement is that, the author has not done any stiatiscal test to establish conclusions about statistical significance. This is an overclaiming results since only basic summary statistics have been computed.
6. The original author claimed that, "The differences in BMI between income groups are statistically significant, which shows that income **determines** BMI". The second problem with this statement is that, the dataset used by the author was a survey data but not a data of experimental design; but to causal claims like, "income **determines** or **causes** BMI", that requires the data collection to come from an experimental design that can rule out alternative explanations for any effects observed. This is also another example of overclaiming results.
